segments.text: If the death of Christ satisfied God, and thereby redeemed the Elect from the curse, then the redemption of souls is costly; souls are dear things, and of great value with God. Ye know (saith the Apostle) that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as Silver and Gold from your vain conversation received by tradition: but with the pretious blood of the Son of God, as of a Lamb without spot. 1 Pet. 1.18, 19. Only the blood of God, is found an equivalant price for the redemption of souls. Gold and silver may redeem from Turkish, but not from Hellish bondage. The whole creation sold to the utmost worth of it, is not a value for the redemption of one soul. Souls are dear ware, he that paid for them, found them so. Yet how cheaply do sinners sell their souls, as if they were but low priz'd Commodities! But you that sell your souls cheap, will buy repentance dear.
